_readme: Declarative registry for the reusable web perf harness. Each scenario names a workload kind (scroll|read|open|search|edit|hover|warm), a repo-relative PDF (portable, from the CC0 test_corpora/dartpdf corpus so any checkout - and any git worktree in an A/B diff - can run it), and kind-specific params passed to the harness via URL query. The driver (driver.mjs) serves `pdf` at /perf.pdf, sets the query from `params`, and merges whatever window.__perfMetrics() returns into the run envelope - so adding a scenario needs NO driver change. Pick one with `node driver.mjs --scenario <name>` or `tool/perf.sh web <name>`; A/B two revisions with `tool/perf.sh webdiff <ref> <name>`.

scroll-plan.note: 16-sheet vector plan set (~70k ops/page). Scroll + fast-fling: frame smoothness and interpret/decode worker offload.

scroll-scan.note: 12p A3 scanned grayscale (~3.7 MB decoded/page). Stresses off-thread image decode + the image cache.

scroll-text.note: 40p office-text report, the everyday reading workload: cheap glyph-only pages scrolled and flung past. Light per page, so what shows up here is scheduling and retention, not interpret throughput.

zoom-scan.note: Deep-zoom settle cycles on A3 scans: the tile pyramid's region-scoped image re-decode. Every page is one big raster, so zoom sharpness comes entirely from re-decoding the visible slice - this is the workload that pays for it.

scroll-diagram.note: 3p ultra-dense diagram (~270k ops/page, MB-scale streams). Tokenizer/interpreter saturation.

scroll-photo-noworker.note: 6p full-page DeviceRGB DCTDecode covers (~1240x1654) with the render worker OFF (worker=0), so every JPEG decodes on the main thread through _decodeOne. The A/B lever for #458's browser-codec fallback vs the engine WASM codec - the win the worker-on desktop path hides.

scroll-cad-labels.note: 6p A3 sheets of 660 UNIQUE survey-point labels each, substituted Helvetica. The run-layout cache misses on every label, so this is the worst case for substituted-text shaping (#454) - the interpret line's shape= vs replay= split shows shaping vs canvas-call volume when the cache cannot help.

open-plan.note: Cold-open time-to-first-content jumping to a heavy vector sheet mid-document.

open-text.note: Cold-open of a 40p office-text doc: page-tree walk + first paint.

open-diagram.note: Cold-open first-content on a ~270k-op/~450KB-content dense diagram: the #527 bounded-early-prefix BASELINE. A/B vs open-diagram-progressive for the #564 reveal (earlyPrefixMin lowered so this just-under-512KB page engages both).

open-diagram-progressive.note: Same cold-open as open-diagram but with the #564 progressive top-down reveal on: the vector-first record streams growing linework prefixes. openFirstContentMs vs open-diagram is the first-content A/B.

search-text.note: Full-document text search latency + match count on a 40p text report (best-of-3). 'Page' hits ~1.1k times, spread across every page - a stable, comparable workload.

hover-ink.note: 240 pointer-hover events over a dense vector sheet with the ink tool armed - the painted pen cursor has to follow the mouse. Measures whether that costs a rebuild of the editing overlay's subtree or a repaint of the cursor layer (#403): watch hoverBuildMsTotal / hoverBuildMsPerEvent.

hover-eraser.note: Same hover sweep with the eraser armed (the ring cursor). Same metrics as hover-ink; a second armed tool so a regression in one cursor path doesn't hide behind the other.

edit-annotate.note: Apply 24 highlight/rectangle/ink annotations through PdfEditingController: incremental-save + appearance-gen cost, revisions, buffer growth.

warm-plan-off.note: Control arm for #614: idle 6s with the idle full-raster warm OFF, then jump to a mid-document sheet. warmArriveMs is what arriving on an unvisited heavy vector sheet costs today.

warm-plan-document.note: Same script with the whole-document idle warm ON. warmArriveMs vs warm-plan-off is the feature's headline win; warmCompletions/warmRetainedMb/warmEvictions are what it spent to get it.

warm-scan-document.note: Scan-heavy arm: 12p A3 grayscale (~3.7 MB decoded/page). Warming these costs image decode, so watch warmRetainedMb and warmEvictions against the budget as well as warmArriveMs.

read-text.note: Read a 40p office-text report page by page, then read back. Every page is cheap, so readFirstSettleP50Ms is pure scheduling latency and readBackInstantPct is how much of the document the caches actually kept - the 'PDFium shows it instantly, we take a moment' shape.

read-booklet.note: Mixed text/graphics booklet read end to end and back. Guards the reading journey on a document whose pages are not uniformly cheap.

read-plan.note: Heavy vector plan set on the same reading journey: the arm that must not regress when scheduling gets greedier - these pages are the ones the one-per-frame pacing exists for.

scroll-hatch.note: 4p A1 sheets, ~70 tiling-pattern-hatched regions each (~300k device commands/page under per-tile re-execution). The #524 record-once/replay anchor: interpret cost, record size, build/raster.
